headline: CGBs edge firmer into month-end as the PBOC adds a redemption backstop; long end leads, belly stays rich
summary: China government bonds firmed slightly on a quiet Monday, even though month-end funding tightened. The CCDC 10-year slipped 0.2bp to 1.638%, a hair above its 1.635% low, and the 30-year led with a 0.5bp fall to 2.062% as TL futures rose 0.29%. The 5-year was flat at 1.353%, so the rich belly did not join in. Policy banks matched CGBs: CDB 10-year at 1.672% is still only about 3bp over, and a strong ADBC auction cleared well below the CCDC curve.
drivers: Month-end funding firms, PBOC smooths it

Tax payments, government bond settlement and month-end pushed Shibor overnight up 3bp to 1.301% and FR007 to 1.405%. The PBOC restarted the 7-day operation (RMB56bn at 1.40%) next to RMB398bn of overnight repos, a RMB116bn net injection. The October MLF rolled RMB700bn against RMB900bn maturing, but RMB400bn of net outright reverse repos this month means medium-term liquidity is still up on the month.

Around 17:00, after the close, the PBOC set up a swap facility. If many funds and wealth products face redemptions at once and the bond market is under systemic stress, large managers can borrow PBOC bills, repo them for cash and buy bonds back from their own funds. It lowers the risk of a sell-off feeding on itself, which helps long bonds and policy bank and credit spreads more than the front end.

Last week brokers sold long bonds to lock in gains, and talk of tax-exemption changes for CGBs also weighed. Today TL futures rose 0.29% to 118.00 while T, TF and TS barely moved. Demand for policy bank paper stayed strong: ADBC sold 5-year bonds at 1.423% and 10-year at 1.649%, with bids covering the offer 8.7 and 9.6 times.

The Fifth Plenum opened today (to Oct 29) focused on party discipline, not stimulus. Stocks were mixed: the Shanghai Composite rose 0.19%, ChiNext fell 2.17%, and turnover dropped to RMB1.62tn. The yuan hit a 4-year high near 6.669 per dollar even though the PBOC fixed it weaker than expected, so FX does not limit easing.
data: RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
Growth is led by exports and AI-linked output, with households and property still weak. It does not challenge low yields.
CPI 0.9% (f 1.0%), core 1.0%; PPI 5.0% (f 4.4–4.5%), highest since Jun 2022
Cost-push from oil and AI components, not demand. Bonds ignore it unless core CPI follows.
New loans RMB1.08tn (f 0.98tn); TSF 3.55tn; M2 7.2% (f 7.4%); M1 3.2%
Loan growth is at a record-low 4.8% and money growth is slowing. Weak credit demand keeps banks buying bonds.
As expected. The policy signal now comes from the overnight-rate switch, not the LPR.
Back above 50. October's print on Oct 31 is the next test for the rally.
view: Range-bound with a mild bullish bias over the next 1–2 weeks. I keep the expected CCDC 10-year range at 1.60–1.68%. The backstop and the coming overnight anchor support bonds, but month-end funding is firmer and regulators have signalled discomfort below about 1.62%. Keep owning the 10-year against the rich 5–7Y belly and against policy banks rather than adding outright duration. An overnight policy rate set at or below 1.25% on Nov 2, or a weak October PMI, would open 1.60%. Strong industrial profits, a pro-growth plenum readout or an equity rebound would push back toward 1.68%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year at 1.243% is in the 11th percentile of its year (average 1.314%), and the 1-year at 1.180% still yields less than overnight funding, which firmed to about 1.29–1.30% today. The front end already prices an overnight policy rate near 1.25% and needs an actual cut to rally further.
buckets.call: Hold; don't chase below 1.20% on the 2-year. Add only if the overnight rate is set below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The 2s5s10s fly is −17.4bp, in the 2nd percentile of the year against a −7.4bp average, and the 5-year (1.353%) and 7-year (1.456%) are near 1-year lows. The 5s10s flattener is open: 28.4bp against a 29bp entry, still on the steep side for the year (71st percentile).
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: In outright terms the 10-year at 1.638% sits at its 1-year low. Against its neighbours it is cheap: the 7s10s20s fly is −24.0bp, in the 86th percentile against a −29.4bp average. That makes it the best value on the curve for duration.
buckets.call: Range 1.60–1.68%. Buy toward 1.665–1.68%; take profit near 1.61%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: 10s30s is 42.5bp, in the 27th percentile and a little below its 45.4bp average. The 30-year at 2.062% bounced today and the new backstop helps, but regulators' warnings and talk of tax changes on CGBs argue against chasing.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is 3.4bp over CGB, in the 2nd percentile against a 10.1bp average, and CDB 2-year and 5-year spreads (11.9bp and 9.6bp) are also at 1-year tights. The switch is open from ~3bp. Today's ADBC auction cleared well through the curve, so demand is still strong, but the RMB800bn of new policy financing tools still has to be funded.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 2.8bp more than CDB, in the 73rd percentile against a 1.2bp average. EXIM is 1.9bp over CDB, about its 2.0bp average. Today's ADBC 10-year auction at 1.649%, bid 9.6 times, shows investors are willing to own the name.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~2–3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 30-year is 11.0bp over CGB, below its 12.8bp average and at the very bottom of its 11.0–16.9bp range for the year, so it is less cheap than it looked last week. The 20-year spread (6.4bp) is already at its 1-year tight.
buckets.call: Neutral; prefer it to policy bank 10Y if you must own policy banks, but don't add below 10bp.

watch: Next: September industrial profits (Oct 27), the Fifth Plenum communiqué (Oct 29), the Fed decision (Oct 28, early Oct 29 Beijing), October PMIs (Sat Oct 31), the end of the overnight repo series and the rate the PBOC sets when it switches (Nov 2), and Hong Kong accepting CGBs as margin collateral from Nov 2.
